extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting research manuscripts to academic journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers preparing manuscripts for journal peer review, focused on common causes of rejection at the peer review stage and practical steps to reduce risk of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient scientific significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Many excellent, elegantly prepared submissions are rejected because they provide only confirmatory results. Nothing novel is offered to further the science. Single case reports on conditions already reported in large studies will often be seen as not sufficiently important. Papers reporting negative results are also usually rejected because journals highly prioritise submissions that report positive results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to pursue and present novel findings or address 'big' questions in your specialty; avoid submitting work that is merely confirmatory or redundant with larger existing studies, and be aware some journals deprioritise negative results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient data upon which to base conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the hypothesis may be clear and the study well designed, conclusions may lack sufficient data to support them — e.g., sample size or patient data set too small to yield statistically significant results, or follow-up period too short to demonstrate claimed efficacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may request additional experiments, enrolment of more patients, or reporting results after a longer follow-up period. Design studies with adequate sample size and follow-up to support the conclusions you intend to draw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient overall quality of manuscript submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers expect authors to submit papers of the highest quality possible; sloppiness or inattention to detail can lead to rejection despite otherwise good science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use available journal reviewer protocols/checklists as an objective framework; invest in careful preparation, consider professional editing or internal review to ensure high overall quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology (rigor of methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may be asked to focus intensely on methodology; the rigor and appropriateness of the methods is a key evaluation dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure methods are well-justified, reproducible, and described in sufficient detail for evaluation; anticipate and address methodological limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical practices / compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical practices are a focus for some reviewers; correct institutional protocols and protections must be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document ethics approvals and consent procedures clearly; consult ethicists or institutional review boards as needed to proactively guard against ethical breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical evaluation is an area some reviewers concentrate on; inadequate or incorrect statistical analysis can prompt rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate statistical methods, clearly report analyses, and consider involving statisticians/biostatisticians or study design experts to calculate sample sizes and validate analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meticulous and accurate statistical calculations and tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical calculations and tables must be meticulous and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check computations, ensure tables are correctly labeled and interpretable, and present summary statistics and uncertainty measures (e.g., confidence intervals, p-values) appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness and clarity in reporting research processes and techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting of research processes and techniques should be thorough and clear so reviewers can evaluate what was done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient procedural detail, protocols, and descriptions so others can assess or reproduce the work; avoid vague or incomplete method descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision in graphics and images
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics and images should be precise and well-designed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, labeled figures; employ graphic artists or visualization best practices when needed to present data optimally and avoid misleading or low-quality visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct grammar and language usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct grammar and language usage are expected; poor language can lead to rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofread carefully, use native-level language quality or professional editing services, and ensure clarity of expression throughout the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to detail and format in the references
rubrics_metrics.description: References must be formatted correctly and attended to in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow journal reference style precisely, ensure all citations are accurate and complete, and check for consistency across the reference list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make sure your hypothesis/research question is significant to your specialty
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should ensure their hypothesis or research question addresses the 'big' questions in their specialty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brainstorm with colleagues and department leadership to identify important problems; design experiments that directly address those problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a wide network to contribute to research and writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Form connections with individuals who can contribute to research and writing, such as statisticians, ethicists, research librarians, and graphic artists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage specialists for sample size calculation and study design (statisticians), ethics oversight (ethicists), literature/search support (research librarians), and visual design (graphic artists); the 'academic village' improves manuscript quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have seasoned mentors read your paper before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Seasoned mentors can provide honest, demanding, and rigorous pre-submission critique that improves the manuscript and can become enthusiastic supporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek rigorous pre-submission evaluation from senior researchers; if unavailable, consider academic editing services that provide scientific assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and execute sufficiently large studies with adequate follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting sufficiently large studies and having adequate follow-up enhances the chances of passing peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan study size and follow-up durations during design to ensure the study can support the claims made; justify these design choices in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit high-quality papers that exude attention to every detail
rubrics_metrics.description: High-quality presentation and meticulous attention to detail across the manuscript increase the likelihood of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to all elements (data, methods, figures, language, references); consider professional review/editing to remove sloppiness that could trigger rejection.
